Script:


VO 1 The National Council of Provinces, or NCOP, has blocked the Western Cape's plan to dissolve the failing Knysna council and place it under administration.

“ Knysna Municipality did not fail to perform its constitutional duties.”

UPSOUND THOMAS KAUNDA/NATIONAL COUNCIL OF PROVINCES
In the opinion of the majority members of the Select Committee, the invocation of section 11 c of the Constitution inthe KNYSNA Local Municipality is not substantively justifiable.

VO 2
It’s a political victory for the ANC-led coalition running Knysna… and a blow to those who say they’re living with the consequences of its collapse. And it’s a story we first brought you over a year ago… a story of a paradise poisoned.

ARCHIVE UPSOUND: Lynn Kayster / Hornlee resident
“We are pushed to the extreme when the frustration builds up. We are trying from our side as the community to assist this municipality and you’re just hitting on closed doors.”

VO 3
Then, as now, the signs of decay were everywhere. Raw sewage flowing into streets and the sensitive Knysna estuary…

ARCHIVE NATSOUND: (Sewage flow)
“We’re going where we need to protect our feet… Erin: From? From sewage”

VO 4 …a water system in crisis… arousing the anger of provincial authorities…
ARCHIVE NATSOUND: (Sewage flow)

UPSOUND: Anton Bredell / MEC for Local Government
"Nobody will be able to swim within that lagoon in December... I will never drink water in Knysna except bottled water."

VO 5
....and a council chamber where chaos trumped governance.

“Are you running council? Shut up man!... They can fucking go to hell.” ARCHIVE NATSOUND: Council meeting

VO 6
Faced with this ongoing collapse, the Western Cape Government finally acted, using the Constitution to dissolve the council and appoint an administrator to take control. At the time, provincial MEC for Local Government, Anton Bredell, said he had no faith in the coalition or its turnaround plan.

UPSOUND: Anton Bredell / MEC for Local Government
"Knysna doesn't suffer with political problems, it suffers from a leadership problem... and those leaders are now in charge of this [support] plan." TIME: 02:26

VO 7
That leadership is headed by mayor, Thando Matika. In the job for less than a year, he asked residents to give the coalition time to reverse the chaos.

ARCHIVE UPSOUND: Thando Matika / Knysna Mayor
For the last 10 years and we keep on saying that is aging infrastructure we keep on saying is financial instability so we are saying that give us time.

VO 9
If nothing improves significantly, it may be too late for an estuary that’s the last refuge for the critically endangered Knysna Seahorse. An ecosystem as fragile as this one relies on proper management.
Small pause
Proper management that’s been sadly lacking, according to the provincial government. It has the power to intervene where local government is failing… or so it thought. Shortly after our last visit this year, Knysna was placed under administration by Bredell and then promptly handed back to the coalition by Parliament.

UPSOUND: Anton Bredell / MEC for Local Government
"We found a body in the reservoir... if that's the quality of services the NCOP is happy with, well then the bar is very, very low."

VO 10
With local government elections just months away, will Knysna has become the ultimate political football.?

VO 11
The municipality is commercially insolvent, and neighbouring towns have had to step in to provide basic services like water and refuse removal.

VO 12
The question is no longer whether the town can be saved from itself, but whether anyone in power, at any level, has the will to put people before politics.

END
